tbilisi-rustavi-ponichala-sutip.whole: ADB's completion report says 3.5 km of the planned 6.8 km of Section 2 was built, and that an existing 3.2 km local road was upgraded instead to join Sections 1 and 3 - a change ADB's Independent Evaluation Department says was never formally recorded as a change of scope. Spending came to $52.98 million against the $118.21 million estimated at approval, and $27.00 million of the $73 million loan was cancelled in September 2019 with a further $11.80 million in April 2021. Three of the four planned breakwaters in the project's second part, coastal protection at Anaklia, were cancelled in 2018; the completion report counts 1.43 km of beach nourishment and one 0.3 km breakwater built. ADB put the economic return on the road at 6.81% at completion against 8.7% at appraisal, below its own 12% threshold, and rated the project less than successful; its evaluation department recomputed the return at 6.7% and rated the wider program less than successful, while ADB's own count of people benefiting was 2.57 million against a 1.45 million target. Every figure here comes from ADB's own documents; no independent check was found.
tbilisi-rustavi-ponichala-sutip.searched: ADB project page 42414-043; ADB Project Completion Report, July 2022 (42414-043-pcr-en.pdf, downloaded with curl and read from disk); ADB Independent Evaluation Department Performance Evaluation Report PE-874, February 2026 (pper_geo_urban_transport_0.pdf, same method). No non-ADB account of what the road delivered was found.

peshawar-landfill-ghari-faiz-ullah.whole: ADB says the five-city project the landfill belongs to is meant to benefit up to 3.5 million people in Abbottabad, Kohat, Mardan, Mingora and Peshawar. By 29 July 2026 ADB's own records show $219.23 million of its $380 million loan under contract and $179.39 million disbursed, $111.41 million of the Asian Infrastructure Investment Bank's $200 million under contract and $49.05 million disbursed, and $3.62 million of the $5 million grant disbursed; the closing date is 30 June 2028. The monitoring report for July-December 2025, prepared for the project, lists the Peshawar solid waste management package (CW-07 Lot 1) as not tendered and not started, puts the Peshawar water supply works at 35.74% complete against 100% planned, and says the Peshawar parks works at Besai Park and Bagh-e-Naran reached 84.10% and were then suspended by the contractors over delayed payments and an unapproved variation order. These figures come only from ADB and the consultants it pays to supervise the works; no independent check was found.
peshawar-landfill-ghari-faiz-ullah.searched: ADB project page 51036-002 (financing, timetable, cumulative contract awards and disbursements for Loan 4160-PAK, Loan 8412-PAK and Grant 0816-PAK); ADB semi-annual environmental monitoring report No. 8, July-December 2025 (51036-002-emr-1155496-en.pdf, downloaded with curl and read from disk) for the contract-by-contract status and physical progress charts. The monitoring report names no figure for waste tonnage handled or for anything built at the Ghari Faiz Ullah site; searches found no non-ADB account of what the project has delivered.

sahiwal-piciip-land-and-sewage.whole: ADB's records show $188.72 million of the $200 million loan under contract and $172.76 million disbursed by 29 July 2026, with the closing date moved from 30 June 2024 to 30 June 2026. The project monitoring report for July-December 2025 puts physical progress in Sahiwal at 75.61% for the North Zone water supply works, 92.67%, 88.60% and 93.04% for the three sewerage lots, and 75.05% for the wastewater treatment plant, whose Rs 2.43 billion contract was signed on 4 June 2024 with completion set for 3 July 2026; it records the supply and installation of water and sanitation equipment, the Sahiwal road upgrading and the park rehabilitation at 100%. The same report says the treatment plant is being built on 199 acres, where ADB's social monitoring reports put the land to be acquired at 196.35 acres. All of these figures come from ADB and its supervision consultants; no independent check was found.

batumi-bypass-land-valuation.whole: ADB's project page describes the works as a new two-lane bypass of 16.2 km around Batumi plus performance-based maintenance of about 200 km of international and secondary roads. Georgia Today reported on 16 October 2024 that a 14-kilometre two-way bypass with 20 bridges and five tunnels had officially opened, put the total project cost at GEL 330 million, and added that some residents said the road was not in fact open to vehicles, which officials denied; no source opened reconciles the 14 km opened with the 16.2 km in ADB's description. ADB put executed works on the bypass at 82% as of 31 December 2023 and expected them to finish in May 2024, and by 12 August 2026 recorded $106.52 million of its $114 million loan disbursed, with the loan closing date moved from 31 December 2023 to 31 December 2026. The length, cost and progress figures all trace back to ADB and to Georgia's Roads Department; no traffic count or independent audit of the finished road was found.
batumi-bypass-land-valuation.searched: ADB project page 50064-001 (scope, progress of executed works, loan utilization, revised closing date); Georgia Today, 16 October 2024, on the opening, the 14 km length, 20 bridges, five tunnels and GEL 330 million cost. interpressnews.ge (25 November 2024) carries only forecasts quoted from AIIB staff, so it was not used. georoad.ge would not serve its monitoring report PDF over curl: TLS error 'self-signed certificate in certificate chain' with the default store, then 'Recv failure: Connection reset by peer' with the proxy CA bundle. 1tv.ge returned a Cloudflare block page (HTTP 403, 'Sorry, you have been blocked').

kolkata-keiip-tranche2-vendors.whole: ADB's project data sheet, last updated 20 March 2024, lists what the tranche built: 28 km of transmission mains, 444 km of distribution mains and 35,242 additional water meters; nine elevated reservoirs holding 17,100 kilolitres and two ground-level reservoirs holding 22 megalitres; 109 km of sewer drainpipes, 7.05 km of it by micro-tunnelling, plus one extra pumping station and 3.50 km of pumping main. It also records 22 citizen service centres across 16 boroughs of the Kolkata Municipal Corporation, a central grievance cell, and 105 corporation officials trained. The project cost $286 million, of which $86 million was counterpart money; $177.35 million of the ADB loan was disbursed, the loan closed on 31 August 2023 and reached financial closing on 14 June 2024, and ADB says spillover works continued afterwards on state funds. ADB has published no completion report for this tranche, and these are ADB's own figures with no independent check found.

malolos-clark-railway-row-pampanga.whole: Nothing on this line is carrying passengers yet. ADB's financing covers 53.1 km of railway - 51.2 km from Malolos to Clark and Clark International Airport, and a 1.9 km extension from Solis to Blumentritt - inside a planned 163 km North-South Commuter Railway, and ADB says it should cut the Metro Manila to Clark journey from the 2-3 hours a bus takes to under an hour. Citing the Department of Transportation's December 2024 progress report, ADB puts overall civil works progress at 46.78%, with the six packages ranging from 4.96% for the Blumentritt package to 86.70% for N-05. The first $1.3 billion loan's closing date was extended to 31 December 2025, the facility's availability period to 31 December 2028, and a second tranche of $1.45 billion approved in April 2025 had $323.78 million, 22%, disbursed by 22 July 2026. These progress and disbursement figures come from the government department building the line and from ADB; no independent verification was found.
malolos-clark-railway-row-pampanga.searched: ADB project pages 52083-001, 52083-002 (package-by-package and overall physical progress as reported to ADB by the Department of Transportation, loan closing extensions) and 52083-003 (tranche 2 financing plan and disbursements). No independent audit of progress was found; the Commission on Audit was not searched beyond general web search.

nis-railway-bypass-min-holding-tenants.whole: The EIB's project sheet describes the work as modernising and reconstructing the existing Nis-Dimitrovgrad railway, about 96 km, and building a railway bypass of about 22 km around Nis, at a total cost of about EUR 502 million with EIB finance of about EUR 341 million; the EU Delegation in Serbia calls the line almost 104 km and the EU's project page puts the bypass at 22.4 km with three new stations, Nis Sever, Pantelej and Vrezina. Nothing is in service: the EIB's December 2025 announcement of a further EUR 100 million loan and EUR 34 million grant says the money is for upgrading the Sicevo-Dimitrovgrad section, electrifying and signalling the route, and building the Nis bypass, and puts total EU support for the section at EUR 342 million, EUR 234 million in loans and EUR 108 million in grants. The EIB expects average speeds to rise from 50 km/h to up to 120 km/h, annual passengers from about 170,000 to about 550,000, and freight from 3.2 million to about 6.2 million tonnes a year. Works were under way by 28 March 2024, when the Serbian president and the EU ambassador visited the site. All of these figures come from the lender and the EU; no completed-section output and no independent check were found.
nis-railway-bypass-min-holding-tenants.searched: EIB project sheet 20160341 (scope, total cost, signature dates); EIB press release of 15 December 2025 on the EUR 134 million package (speeds, passenger and freight projections, EUR 342 million total); EU Delegation page europa.rs of 28 March 2024 (104 km line, works visit); EU 'EU za tebe' project page (22.4 km bypass, three stations). No figure for track laid, electrified or opened was found in any of them.

bogota-metro-line1-predios.whole: The line is 23.9 km with 16 stations, from the depot at Bosa to Calle 72 at Avenida Caracas, and is not yet running. Bogota's city government said overall works reached 83.73% in September 2026, with 16 km of viaduct built by 19 July 2026 and 20 of the 30 trains in the country; each train is 134 metres long with six cars and room for 1,800 people, and the city says the Bosa to Calle 72 trip will take 27 minutes against up to two hours today, with trial running from September 2027 and commercial operation contracted for 14 March 2028. A monitoring report by the city's own Contraloria Distrital, reported by Publimetro on 22 September 2026, found the road network and public space component 48% behind schedule and the systems and equipment and the stations and access buildings components 18% behind each, and counted 16 changes to the execution plan that had not moved the dates for testing or opening; the Empresa Metro de Bogota's manager said the contractual dates had not changed.

mattala-airport-forest-elephants.whole: The airport has a 3,500-metre runway 60 metres wide, rated to take aircraft as large as the A380, a 12,000 square metre terminal, eight aircraft stands, 12 check-in counters and capacity for one million passengers and 45,000 tonnes of cargo a year, figures given by Airport & Aviation Services (Sri Lanka) to Echelon in 2020, when the same official said there had been zero passenger arrivals in January 2020 and that charter flights for ship crew changes brought about 4,000 passengers and 85 aircraft movements over four and a half months. Airport & Aviation Services and the Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation said 2025 was the airport's busiest year since it opened in 2013, with 140,614 passengers and 703 international flights. A review by Sri Lanka's Auditor-General, reported by the Daily Mirror in January 2026, found 321,577 passengers in total over six years against the projection of one million a year, net losses of Rs 39.3 billion over those six years and capital spending above Rs 36.5 billion, while the company's 2024 annual report showed operating income of Rs 242.2 million against operating costs of Rs 3.6 billion.
mattala-airport-forest-elephants.searched: Echelon, 2 October 2020, 'Mattala airport buzzes after covid' (runway and terminal specifications, capacity, 2020 charter traffic, quotes from AASL's director of operations); The Bangladesh Monitor report of AASL and Ministry of Ports and Civil Aviation figures for 2025 (140,614 passengers, 703 international flights); Daily Mirror, 13 January 2026, 'Mattala Airport accumulates Rs.39bn in losses as govt. pivots to new PPP model' (Auditor-General review and AASL 2024 annual report figures) - this page's body is loaded by script and did not come through curl, so it was read with WebFetch. ft.lk articles returned only page furniture over curl, with the article body script-loaded.
